title: Fewshot contrast fieldnotes
content:
Purpose / context:
- Personal fieldnotes for a focused experiment set: contrastive few-shot configurations. Trying to map which small changes in example selection/order/labeling flip model behavior. Keep informal; dump experiments and quick triage outcomes here.

Background summary:
- Using hosted-api default 'gpt-like' open model family (internal alias: oak-7b) for most tests. Running localized small-batch eval harness (100-250 examples) to get quick signal; follow-ups to be run on standardized eval infra.
- Problem: some templates that look identical to humans show wildly different hallucination rates when we swap benign negative examples in the shot set. Need rules-of-thumb for catalog templates.

Top-level hypotheses:
1) Contrastive pairs (one positive canonical example + one near-miss counterexample) reduce hallucination for factual-retrieval tasks but increase false-negatives on permissive QA.
2) Example order matters most when the target instruction is short/ambiguous. For longer, explicit instructions order effect shrinks.
3) Negative-example injection (showing a "bad answer" example) helps reduce terse confident hallucinations but increases abstain-like responses.

Experiments run (quick log):
- exp-2025-11-10-A: customer-email-classification
  config: 3-shot: [clean-ticket, near-duplicate, negative-mislabel]
  prompt framing: "Given email => output: {category}"
  outcome: accuracy up 6% vs baseline; precision up; recall down ~4%. Notes: model became conservative for "billing" vs "subscription" borderline cases.

- exp-2025-11-19-B: SQL-synthesis (NL->SQL)
  config: 2-shot contrastive (one correct, one subtly wrong join)
  outcome: syntactic correctness same; semantic correctness (execution match) -4% when wrong join shown second. Hypothesis: model overweighted the faulty example pattern.

- exp-2025-12-02-C: factual QA (short questions)
  config: 4-shot with 2 negative examples (plausible but false facts) interleaved
  outcome: hallucination rate reduced from 21% -> 11%, but abstain/"I don't know" rose from 2% -> 9%.

Failure cases observed (examples):
- example: instruction "List three features of product X" with contrastive shot that lists features + subtle wrong fact -> model lists fewer items or exactly reproduces the wrong fact under different wording.
- example: code-suggestion use case: when negative example demonstrates insecure pattern, sometimes model flips to replicating the insecure pattern rather than avoiding it. Possibly due to label signals not explicit (we only show example inputs/outputs, not "good/bad" flags).

Quick heuristics (working):
- If you care about recall (surface all relevant candidates), avoid negative examples; prefer positive diversity.
- If you need conservative answers (reduce hallucinations), include 1-2 explicit negative examples but also label them with short comment like "(incorrect)" or add a short meta-instruction: "Avoid repeating incorrect examples."
- Keep near-miss negatives temporally separated (place them before the final canonical example) — seemed to help in a few tests.

Template variants to keep / expand: (raw drafts)
- Template A (contrastive pair, labeled):
  "You are an assistant. Examples:
   Input: ...
   Output: ...
   Note: incorrect example (do not follow)
  Now answer: <USER_INPUT>"

- Template B (meta-instruction after shots):
  "Examples show good and bad outputs. Use the pattern from the correct examples only."

- Template C (separator-strong):
  Use a heavy delimiter ("---EXAMPLE---") between shots; reduces bleeding of token-level patterns in oak-7b.

Open questions / weird artifacts:
- Why does oak-7b sometimes latch onto the *second* example pattern preferentially? Is there a recency bias with our SDK batching? Need to check request tokenization order (are we inadvertently reversing the shot order in some SDK helper?). Filing RED-912 to track.
- Do negative examples need explicit labels? We have mixed signals: unlabeled negatives sometimes backfire.
- Interaction with system messages: adding a short system instruction "do not invent facts" didn't uniformly help; needs per-task tuning.

Mini checklist before formalizing into eval harness:
- [ ] Re-run top 3 experiments with 1k examples each on dedicated infra (remove sampling noise)
- [ ] Add explicit "(incorrect)" label variant to negative exs and compare
- [ ] Run same templates across oak-7b/cedar-13b (different families) to test model-family sensitivity
- [ ] Create small toy dataset that isolates "near-join" SQL bug to measure param effect

Notes to self (messy):
- Keep these raw notes. When we have consistent patterns, fold into "prompt-library-guides/contrastive-notes" in Confluence.
- Tomas: follow up on SDK tokenization order (Slack thread #sdk-chat).
- Rina: try explicit-label negative examples and push quick PR to eval harness.

Quick examples to copy into tests (copy/paste ready) :
- QA (few-shot)
  EX1 Input: "Who painted Starry Night?"
  EX1 Output: "Vincent van Gogh"
  EX2 Input: "Who painted Sunrise at Sea?"
  EX2 Output: "John Doe (incorrect)"
  >>> Test Input: "Who painted Starry Night?"  >>> target: "Vincent van Gogh" (avoid repetition of mislabeled facts)
- SQL example
  EX1 Input: "List customers with more than 3 orders"
  EX1 Output: "SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;"
  EX2 Input: "List customers with > 3 orders"
  EX2 Output: "SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE orders_count > 3; -- wrong if there's no denorm field"

Telemetry / metrics to capture on future runs:
- hallucination_rate (manual label / heuristics)
- abstain_rate
- exact_match / execution_match (for SQL)
- per-class precision/recall (for classification)
- example-order sensitivity score (new: fraction of outputs that change when reversing shot order)
- latency (tokens/sec) — check if heavy separators increase tokenization overhead / latency

Quick log of followups:
- 2026-02-20: added explicit-label negative example test (local run, 200 examples) => hallucination down, abstain up. Save results in linked GH PR.
- 2026-02-25: found that oak-7b SDK helper had a bug that reversed shot list when using example-builder v0.3. Repro steps in RED-912.

Final short thought: contrastive few-shot is powerful but brittle. Our immediate product guidance should be pragmatic: provide 2 template families in prompt-library ("high-recall" and "low-hallucination") with clear notes and toggles for negative-example labeling. Don't ship ambiguous unlabeled negatives as default.

-- E.P.
notes_summary: scratchpad for contrastive few-shot experiments; observed tradeoffs between hallucination and recall; actionable checklist to formalize into eval runs
